Bond University College Foundation Progr.curriculum: The Foundation Program is organised as a set of subject strands rather than a standard degree major, delivered as eight 10-credit-point subjects taught in small classes over about nine to ten months: BCFN01-003 Foundation Mathematics 1 (bringing quantitative skills up to university entry standard), BCFN01-010 Foundation English 1 and BCFN01-012 Foundation English 2 (academic reading, writing, speaking and listening), BCFN01-021 Foundation Mathematics 2 (probability and statistics, functions, geometry, trigonometry and differential calculus for students heading into health sciences, construction or business), BCFN01-022 Modern History (major conflicts and ideological forces from 1914 to the present), BCPP01-001 Communication and Culture 1 and BCPP01-002 Communication and Culture 2 (media, rhetoric, academic writing and referencing, extended to World War I and II and Civil Rights case studies), and BCPP01-003 Digital Solutions (digital literacy and multimedia skills for university study). There is no elective choice: all students complete the same subject set before progressing into a Bond bachelor's degree.

English.description: English language courses run by Bond University College for international students who need to reach the English standard for entry to a Bond degree, diploma or foundation program. Classes are full time and taught in mixed-ability groups at a level matched to each student, covering academic reading, writing, listening and speaking (including pronunciation) plus critical thinking, research skills and the technology and discussion-based learning style used at Bond. The program is officially classified by Bond as a Non-AQF award (program code CO-00023, CRICOS code 103878M), not a degree, diploma or certificate. Subjects run in two formats: standard 10-week blocks and a shorter 4-week Portfolio format, both scheduled several times a year. On reaching the required level, students progress directly into their target Foundation, diploma or degree program. It suits international students who are close to, but not yet at, the English standard for their intended Bond program.
English.curriculum: Bond English has no fixed subject list in the way an academic degree does; instead it is organised as academic English classes at different proficiency levels, covering reading, writing, listening and speaking (including pronunciation) plus critical thinking and research skills, run in mixed-ability classes so students of varying levels are taught together with individualised attention. Two subject formats are scheduled on the program's own timetable: standard English subjects that run for 10 weeks, and a shorter English Portfolio format that runs for 4 weeks, both offered multiple times a year (2025, 2026 and 2027 intake dates are published on Bond's own site). Program length and level depend on where a student starts and their target program, with outcomes and scheduling designed to lead directly into a Bond University College Foundation Program or diploma, or a Bond undergraduate or postgraduate degree.
English.admission_requirements: Entry to the English program itself requires a result from one of the following English-language tests, no older than 24 months at the time of commencement: IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge English: Advanced, or Pearson Versant. The result places the applicant at the appropriate starting level within the program rather than granting entry to a fixed single level.
English.english_requirements: No single published minimum score gates entry to the program itself: applicants apply with a result from IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge English: Advanced, or Pearson Versant (no older than 24 months at commencement), and that result is used to place them at the appropriate proficiency level within Bond English, with progression tied to reaching the English standard required for their target Bond program rather than a single fixed entry score.

Graduate Diploma in Business.curriculum: The Graduate Diploma in Business carries no fixed core subjects of its own on Bond's live subjects page; instead the whole eight-subject, two-semester program is built from two elective pools: the Bond Business School Postgraduate Electives pool (any Bond Business School postgraduate subject) and the University Postgraduate Electives pool (any postgraduate subject across the University that is offered as a general elective), with 40 credit points required from postgraduate subjects across the University subject to meeting prerequisites. In practice students typically take introductory business subjects such as accounting, marketing and finance from the Business School pool, all of which are credited in full toward the Master of Business for students who continue.

Graduate Diploma in Construction Practic.curriculum: The Graduate Diploma in Construction Practice is an eight-subject, two-semester program built from a common core plus two elective streams. Core subjects include SSUD71-101 Understanding Buildings (the construction process, stakeholders and cost factors, focused on detached housing), SDCM71-316 Structures and Materials (structural engineering fundamentals and soil mechanics for non-engineering backgrounds), SSUD71-103 Principles of Project Management (using the PMBOK Guide framework), SSUD71-308 Project Contract Administration (construction contract law and practice), SSUD71-309 Building Services (electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, fire and vertical-transport systems), SSUD71-313 Commercial Construction and Engineering, and SSUD71-317 Measurement 1 (the Standard Method of Measurement of Building Works). Students then choose 20 credit points from an elective set covering SDCM71-314 Building Controls and Regulation, SDCM71-322 Building Pathology and Forensic Engineering, SDCM71-323 Expert Witness and Dispute Resolution, SDCM71-324 Sustainable Refurbishment and Retrofit, SSUD71-106 Real Estate Property Rights, and SSUD71-300 Planning and Assessment Processes. All subjects are credited in full toward the Master of Construction Practice for students who continue; this Graduate Diploma is listed by Bond as a postgraduate exit-only award, taken by students progressing out of the Master's rather than a direct-entry standalone qualification.

Master of Marketing (Professional).curriculum: The coursework core (about two-thirds of the program) runs through nine subjects: MKTG71-100 Marketing Fundamentals, MKTG71-205 Consumer Experiences and Behaviours, MKTG71-302 Integrated Marketing Communications, MKTG71-303 Market Research, MKTG71-312 Digital Marketing for Customer Engagement, MKTG71-315 Marketing Analytics, MKTG71-320 Strategic Marketing, STAT71-111 Business Statistics and STAT71-112 Quantitative Methods. The remaining roughly one-third of the program is University Postgraduate Electives, which can instead be replaced with an optional 40-credit-point Specialisation (for example in data analytics), plus optional Postgraduate Opportunities such as an international study tour or internship taken as a general elective, subject to GPA, language and prerequisite eligibility. The Professional version then adds a compulsory 20-week Work Integrated Learning placement and professional portfolio in the final semester, on top of the standard Master of Marketing coursework sequence, and is open to international students only.

Master of Philosophy.curriculum: The MPhil has no taught-subject curriculum; its entire structure is a single research subject, Thesis for Master of Philosophy, in which the candidate develops independent research skills and relates a specific research topic to a broad framework of knowledge, with a major emphasis on independent inquiry, research methodology and depth in the topic area rather than any coursework units.
Master of Philosophy.admission_requirements: To be eligible for enrolment, applicants must hold a degree in a relevant subject area from a recognised tertiary institution, with a Cumulative Percent Average (CPA) of at least 65% in the major study area at Australian Bachelor degree level or equivalent, or higher. All Higher Degree by Research applicants, including MPhil candidates, must also submit a detailed Research Project Proposal covering the research topic, methodology, key literature and research questions, prepared with the support of a proposed supervisor, who together with the candidate's faculty assesses whether appropriate supervision and resources exist and whether the proposal has enough merit to justify the degree.
Master of Philosophy.english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0 (or the equivalent PTE/TOEFL score), per Bond's standard international English-language tier; the higher 7.0 tier that Bond publishes for AHPRA-registered professional programs does not apply to the MPhil.
